note: One Scottie 1 picture (256 lines at 48 kHz, 255 lines consumed) takes ~827 ms. About 475 ms of that is goertzel_batch's Python per-sample recurrence, once per line for the mid-line sync search; the rest is three Hilbert FM demods per line. An lfilter or FFT Goertzel keeps the same energies and should remove most of that half.

24 h ISS prediction for London with the default 30-point trajectory and 60-point ground track. The same call with both tracks off is 4.4 ms; the tracks are one skyfield .at() per point (4 passes). Passing each pass's sample times as one array should reclaim most of the ~46 ms.

Called on each RX burst, capped at 2 s at the default 2 Msps (8 MB cs8). ~61 ms is two full-array partitions (median and 95th percentile) of 4e6 amplitudes, then the result is downsampled to 128 bins. A histogram quantile on integer I^2+Q^2 keeps the same order statistics; a stride-then-quantile sketch of the same shape is ~4 ms.

End-of-sweep clustering for 200 BLE devices (six adverts each), the call routes/tscm makes when a sweep stops. Similarity recomputes RSSI and interval stats via statistics.mean/variance, which uses exact rational arithmetic (about a million as_integer_ratio calls in a profile) and rebuilds cluster UUID sets every comparison. Plain sums and cached cluster features should remove most of the ~215 ms.

HackRF waterfall frame at 20 Msps / 25 fps (800k pairs). Peak tracemalloc is 12.87 MiB for a 6.4 MiB complex64 result: the int8 buffer is copied to float32, divided, then promoted through a complex multiply. Writing int8 into one complex64 array and scaling in place, as cu8_to_complex already does, peaks at about 6.4 MiB.
